rationale: Needs both Talarico (TX) and El-Sayed (MI) to win per AP. Talarico leads every recent poll by 1-4 (Emerson +2, Marist +2, TPOR +4), but Texas polls have overstated Democrats in 2018/2020/2024, so ~0.50; El-Sayed leads MI averages by 2-4, ~0.68; results are correlated, joint ~0.38. What would make this wrong: a uniform late Republican polling miss (most likely failure, ~35%), already largely priced in; a market-price result appeared in MI search and was discarded.

Base rate: Democrats have won every MN Senate race since 2002. Flanagan leads Tafoya by 3-5 in averages (RCP 46.6-43.2; SurveyUSA +3; even R pollsters +3); Cook moved to Lean D due to fraud-scandal attacks. Most likely way wrong: undecideds break R in an open-seat race with a weaker candidate (~12%), consistent with this number.

ECB hiked 25bp in September to 2.50% DFR; latest reporting (Oct 26) says rates pricing strongly favors a hold on Oct 29 with hikes seen as unlikely. Base rate: back-to-back hikes when pricing implies a hold are rare. Most likely way wrong: a hawkish surprise on high inflation (~4%). A search result quoting prediction-market odds was seen and discarded.

YES requires no Israeli or Iranian air/missile strike impacting the other's territory through Nov 15. The April ceasefire has held against direct strikes, but NPR/The Hill report US and Israel planning possible strikes in early November after the US midterms (Nov 3) and Israel's Oct 27 election, and Trump says he is choosing between a deal and 'finishing the job'. Most likely way wrong: Trump keeps delaying while talks via Pakistan continue (~40%), so I stay near the middle rather than lower.

SC is a strong R state (Trump +18 in 2024); the Republican leads by ~2 in polling averages, with Andrews massively outraising. In 2020 Graham-Harrison polled close and Graham won by 10, a precedent for polls understating Republicans here. Most likely way wrong: a genuine D wave plus funding edge (~20%). A market price was shown in search results and discarded.

Acton leads Ramaswamy in most October polls (Marist +7, CNN +8, Fox +2; averages +2.6 to +4.4) and Sabato moved it to Lean D on Oct 22. But Ohio polls overstated Democrats in 2016-2024 (e.g., Brown 2024), and Ohio leans R. Most likely way wrong: a 4-5 point polling miss toward R (~30-35%). A market price appeared in a search result and was discarded.

Republicans hold 53 seats; Democrats need net +4. Nate Silver's model gives Democrats ~75% for the Senate as of Oct 19, with Democrats leading in TX, AK and other targets. Most likely way wrong: a systematic polling miss toward R in TX/AK/SC-type states that holds several close seats (~28%), which matches this number.

Needs a general, mutually agreed Russia-Ukraine ceasefire by Oct 31. Only a local Oleshky humanitarian truce (location-specific, does not qualify) was agreed; the next talks are set for mid-November in Abu Dhabi and Russia rejects any pause before a full deal. Five days left; most likely way wrong is a surprise Trump-brokered announcement (~2%).

Peltola leads Sullivan by ~1-3 points in averages and in RCV final-round polls; Trump is rallying for Sullivan. Alaska polls have historically understated Republicans (Sullivan 2020 won by ~13 vs single-digit polls), and incumbency helps. Most likely way wrong: Peltola's lead is real in a D-leaning year (~60%), so I stay below 0.5 but not far. A result quoting market odds was seen and discarded.

Needs an anthropic.com/news announcement of Fable 5.5 by Oct 31. As of an Oct 6 model list, the latest Fable is 5.1 (recent successor to Fable 5), while Opus/Sonnet/Haiku 5.5 are out; a further Fable jump within weeks is unusual for the top tier. Search budget ran out, so no direct news check; most likely way wrong is a same-cycle Fable 5.5 launch to match the 5.5 lineup (~8%).

YES = no qualifying US-Iran Hormuz agreement announced by Nov 2. Talks have been stalled for weeks; Iran says Hormuz stays closed until its seven conditions are met and the US is preparing post-midterm strike options. Base rate for a signed deal in a one-week window amid stalemate is very low. Most likely way wrong: a pre-election surprise deal Trump announces (~5%).

Needs both Saudi Arabia and the Houthis to announce acceptance of a general ceasefire by Oct 31. Fighting escalated in October (Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport, Saudi-backed offensive); there are reports of a $1B Iran-brokered offer, but Riyadh reportedly rejects a new ceasefire before territory is returned. Five days left; most likely way wrong is a quick deal from the Tehran channel (~8-10%).
